packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-10 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING (blind first reading)

Exposure statement: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification of
the work or author, or any earlier reading of these images. I opened only
PROMPT.md and the image files of this packet. (A directory listing showed that a
packet.json exists; I did not open it.) I read packet-08 immediately before
this one in the same session; that packet's strips were not identified either.

Working notes are appended image by image; the layout survey, selection
statement and limitations are consolidated at the end of this file.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
image-001.jpg  (reduced overview)
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Observation: a small bound volume photographed closed, lying with its spine to
the right, beside a cm rule and a colour chart. By the rule the cover is about
15 cm tall and about 10 cm wide. The cover is in two parchment pieces:
 (a) LEFT c. two thirds: a dark, heavily abraded and stained parchment (board
     covering) on which many horizontal lines of small script show as rows of
     brown blotches; at least 30 lines can be counted as bands; a few red
     touches low on the left (about 5-6 cm on the rule).
 (b) RIGHT c. one third, running over the spine: a paler, cleaner parchment
     strip. On it, near its left side, three short groups of script in brown
     ink, each only 4-8 letters wide: one group at the top (cut by the top
     edge, 2-3 lines), a second just below (3 lines with a gap), and a third
     about half-way down (3 lines). The rest of the strip looks blank; faint
     pinkish offset or show-through in its lower part.
The script on both pieces runs horizontally in the photograph's orientation
(upright). No running title, rubric or initial can be made out at this scale.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
image-002.jpg  (native tile: upper left of the cover, piece (a))
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Observation: surface so abraded/stained that the writing survives only as rows
of brown ink blotches; line pitch is visible (about 25-30 lines in this tile)
but I cannot resolve a single secure word. A short row of RED dots/dashes at
the upper left (about level with the first text line) may be the remains of a
rubric, a red line-filler or red underlining - cannot tell. A wormhole upper
centre; a raised lump and holes at the left edge (fastening/tie point?).
image-002: all lines [illegible] - leaf surface, not lack of effort; I looked
for letter shapes along each band and found only isolated ascenders.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
image-003.jpg  (native tile: upper right of the cover; right edge of piece (a) and upper part of spine strip (b))
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Left half of the tile = piece (a): abraded, [illegible]; one clear greenish-black
letter-like mark near the top ("G"? - possibly later ink or a stain), not part
of a readable line.

Right half = spine strip (b). The writing sits in a narrow block at the left
side of the strip, apparently a set of short notes each a few letters wide
(tentative interpretation: marginal annotations or the cut-off line-ends/starts
of a column; the left boundary is where strip (b) overlaps piece (a), so text
may continue underneath).

 Group 1 (top of strip, cut by the upper edge):
image-003 l.1   [ ...illegible, only feet of letters at the edge... ]
image-003 l.2   ut eq̃uuu?            (minims after "eq"/"cq"; "ut eq(ui)..."? uncertain)
image-003 l.3   ꝑis? . ⁊ C . l . ſi   (first word uncertain "pis"/"dis"/"ois"; then Tironian et,
                                     "C" and "l" each followed by a punctus, then "ſi" - reads like an
                                     abbreviated reference; tentative)
 (gap of about one line)
 Group 2:
image-003 l.4   quãq̃.?               (q-u-a with macron, q with mark, punctus; "qua(m)q(uam)."?/"quia q(uod)"?)
image-003 l.5   Jtem                 ("Item", initial I/J with a tail)
 (gap of about one line)
image-003 l.6   fač . l . de?        (or "ſatꝫ. dc"; "fac"/"ſat" with a mark, then "l." and "de"/"dc" -
                                     again like an abbreviated reference)
 (blank for about 8-9 line-heights)
 Group 3:
image-003 l.7   metat'.?             (or "mctatꝰ."; minims + "etat" + abbreviation flourish, punctus)
image-003 l.8   l . deue?            ("l." then "deue"/"deiic")
image-003 l.9   rum ſ?               (bottom edge of tile, cut; "runi ſ"/"rum ſ")

----------------------------------------------------------------------
image-004.jpg  (native tile: lower left of the cover, piece (a))
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Observation: same abraded surface. Horizontal bands of writing are visible in
the upper two thirds (about 18-20 lines); the lowest quarter looks blank
(lower margin of the reused leaf? tentative). Features:
- about a third of the way down, left of centre, RED ink remains over two
  lines: scattered red letter fragments, the first perhaps a capital ("G"/"E"/
  "S"-like shape) followed by dots - the remains of a short rubric or red
  heading, about 3-4 cm long; no letter is securely readable.
- one darker word-shaped group in brown/greenish ink in the fourth or fifth
  visible band, centre ("B...el"/"Pred"? - shapes only, not a reading).
- a torn, lifted patch with a leather/thong stub at the left edge (tie or
  clasp anchor), and thin diagonal scratches.
image-004: all text lines [illegible]; I could not resolve any word with enough
confidence to transcribe. The band just below the red traces shows a row of
minims and one or two ascenders (about 10-12 letters) but stays unreadable.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
image-005.jpg  (native tile: lower right of the cover; piece (a) at left, lower spine strip (b) at right)
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Left half = piece (a): abraded, [illegible]; vertical ridges (spine-side
creasing) run through it.

Right half = spine strip (b):
 Group 3 again (overlap with image-003 l.7-9, not new text), here complete:
image-005 l.1   metat'.?             (= image-003 l.7; minims + "etat"/"ctat" + rising abbreviation
                                     flourish, punctus. First letters could be "in"/"m"/"ui")
image-005 l.2   l . deue?            (= image-003 l.8; "l." then "deue"/"deiic"/"dene")
image-005 l.3   rum ſ?               (= image-003 l.9; "rum"/"tum"/"runi", then long s or "ſ."/"ff"-like sign)
 Below group 3: no further brown-ink writing on the strip. A pale PINK patch
 (about 4 cm tall) covers the middle of the strip under group 3; within it are
 faint vertical and horizontal pale strokes that look like offset or
 show-through of larger red letters or decoration - no letter can be read.
 Faint greenish traces lower right. Yellow-brown tide-line staining along the
 right (spine) edge; torn edge lower right.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
image-006.jpg  (reduced overview, other cover; spine now at the left)
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Observation: the other board of the same volume. From left to right:
 - the pale spine strip (b) wrapping round, blank here apart from yellow
   staining; its lower half is covered by a torn patch of paper/thin parchment
   with a ragged hole, on which a large later cursive word is written sideways
   (reading upward), cut by the tear ("...reg..."?/"...eg" - shapes only).
 - a middle band of pale paper or parchment pasted over the board (about 3 cm
   wide, torn away at lower right) carrying LATER CURSIVE handwriting written
   SIDEWAYS (rotated 90 degrees; lines run bottom-to-top), in brown ink: several
   long vertical pen strokes (descenders/flourishes of large letters), a large
   word that looks like "pan..les"/"parolles"? reading upward near the left of
   the band, and a smaller line reading upward nearer the centre
   ("...toleos de ... +"? - very tentative). This is a different, later hand
   from the gothic book hand on the other cover, and is not manuscript waste
   text in the same sense (it may be a title/ownership note or reused document).
 - at the right, the dark abraded board covering (same kind of surface as
   piece (a)), with two tie/clasp stubs; a small red mark near the top right;
   a short line of faint later ink near the bottom ("....." unreadable at this
   scale).
No columns, running titles or initials can be determined.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
image-007.jpg  (native tile: upper right of this cover - fore-edge side)
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Observation: dark abraded parchment over the board; an embossed/blind-ruled
frame line follows the top and right edges. No lines of writing can be resolved
at all in this tile - only mottled staining. A small RED mark (two or three
short strokes, like "ii"/a paragraph sign fragment) near the top right. A
tie/clasp stub (folded parchment or leather tag) centre right. At the lower
left the torn corner of the pasted pale sheet.
image-007: no transcribable text.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
image-008.jpg  (native tile: lower right of this cover - fore-edge side)
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Observation: dark abraded parchment over the board, blind frame line along the
right and bottom edges, second tie/clasp stub at centre. No gothic book-hand
lines can be resolved. Near the bottom, a horizontal row of orange-brown
ink/stain dashes about 4 cm long (the "faint later ink line" of the overview) -
it may be a rubbed line of writing or a stain line; no letter is readable.
image-008: no transcribable text.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
image-009.jpg  (separate close-up photograph, soft focus: a lifted/folded flap of parchment with decoration)
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Observation: a different kind of image - a hand-held close-up, not a tile of
the cover overviews. It shows a folded-back flap of pale parchment (apparently
a turn-in or lifted piece of the binding), black background at the right.
Three distinct things carry writing:

 (i) Far left, on a flat sheet under the flap: two lines of PRINTED italic
     type (from the printed book inside the binding, not manuscript):
image-009 (print) l.1   ...ſaria.        (end of a word; "-saria."/"-faria.")
image-009 (print) l.2   ſunt ſecūdę,     ("sunt secu(n)dę," with macron over u and e-caudata/æ; comma after)
     I transcribe these only because they are visible; they belong to the host
     book, not to the waste.

 (ii) Upper centre/right, on a parchment surface behind the flap: four or five
     lines of a LARGER, darker gothic hand, strongly blurred and partly hidden
     by the fold. Only one group is half-legible:
image-009 (large hand) l.2   ...mex? / ...ntex? ...   (letters about twice the size of the small hand below)
     other lines: [illegible - out of focus and covered by the fold]

 (iii) Centre right, on the flap itself along its right edge: a painted INITIAL
     and five short lines of small gothic book hand in grey-brown ink.
     Initial: a blue letter, about two lines tall and c. 1 cm wide, with white
     reserved vertical stripes carrying red hair-lines, flat base, rounded top;
     its top is hidden by the fold and its right side is at the flap edge. Red
     pen-flourishing descends from its lower left corner in a long double
     line with a small ring at the top and hooked ends, running down the margin
     for about six line-heights; a small blue ring beside it. The letter form
     is uncertain: three vertical members with rounded top would suit an
     uncial M (or a U/V or N seen partially); I cannot decide.
     Text to the right of / below the initial (each line cut on the right by
     the flap edge after 4-6 letters; left side complete at the margin):
image-009 l.1   uuic? [...]          (directly under the base of the initial; minims, "uuic"/"auic"/"unic")
image-009 l.2   ĩciru? [...]         (a superscript "o" stands above the start of this line; then minims with a
                                     macron + "citu"/"ſitu"/"icru")
image-009 l.3   eq̃ꝛ e? [...]         (or "cq̃ꝛ c"; e/c, q with abbreviation, a 2-shaped sign (round r or "-ur"), then e/c)
image-009 l.4   uiſti? [...]         (or "niſti"/"uiſu"; minims + long s + t)
image-009 l.5   eq̃ i.? [...]         (or "cq̃ i:"; similar opening to l.3; ends with a point or two points)
     Above the initial, at the flap edge, the feet of one more line of the same
     small hand: [illegible, 3-4 minims].

----------------------------------------------------------------------
image-010.jpg  (enlarged crop of image-009: the initial and the five lines)
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Overlap: this is the same area as image-009 (iii), enlarged; it adds no new
text, and the enlargement is softer rather than sharper.
image-010 l.1   uuic? [...]          (= image-009 l.1; here the group looks like "auic"/"unic" with the last
                                     letter cut by the edge)
image-010 l.2   ĩ c̊itu? [...]        (= image-009 l.2; superscript ring/o above the second or third letter;
                                     "i(n) ci(r)cu..."?/"icitu" - not resolvable)
image-010 l.3   eq̃ꝛ e? [...]         (= image-009 l.3)
image-010 l.4   uiſti? [...]         (= image-009 l.4; a pale spot/hole in the middle of the word)
image-010 l.5   eq̃ i.? [...]         (= image-009 l.5)
     The initial is clearer here: solid blue ground/body, two white stripes
     each with a pair of red vertical hair-lines, the body narrowing slightly
     toward a flat foot. Red flourish: an angular hook at the upper left, then
     a ring and a triple line running straight down the margin, ending in a
     hook. A grey-blue smudge (offset?) lies left of the flourish.

======================================================================
CONSOLIDATED LAYOUT SURVEY (image-only)
======================================================================
Observations
- Images 001-005 show one cover of a small volume (c. 15 x 10 cm); images
  006-008 the other cover; 009-010 are a soft-focus close-up of a flap with a
  decorated initial, whose position on the binding is not shown.
- Cover 1 carries manuscript waste in two pieces: a heavily abraded leaf over
  the board with c. 30+ lines of small script running horizontally (upright in
  the photo) plus remains of a short red heading low on the left and a red
  dotted trace at top left; and a cleaner spine strip with three short groups
  of small gothic script, 4-8 letters wide, separated by blank gaps.
- Cover 2 shows no readable book hand: abraded board covering, a pasted sheet
  with later cursive written sideways, and a torn patch with a large later
  cursive word.
- The close-up shows a two-line blue initial with red pen-flourishing and
  five line-beginnings of small gothic hand, a second larger gothic hand
  behind, and printed italic text of the host book.
- No running title, column division, underlining or interlinear gloss can be
  established anywhere; the abraded leaf may be single- or double-column, but
  the tiles do not let me see an intercolumnar gap.

Tentative interpretations (flagged)
- The three short groups on the spine strip, each a few abbreviated words with
  "l." and "C." between puncti and an "Item", read like short marginal notes
  or references standing in a margin, with the main text column lost or hidden
  under the overlap. They might equally be the ends of lines of a narrow
  column. I cannot decide from these images.
- The small hand at the initial (009-010) is similar in scale to the spine-strip
  hand, but the focus is too soft to say whether it is the same hand or the
  same leaf.

SELECTION STATEMENT
- Read in full: all writing on the spine strip (image-003 l.1-9, repeated at
  image-005 l.1-3); the five lines at the initial (image-009/010); the two
  printed lines visible in image-009.
- Looked at closely but unreadable: every line of the abraded leaf on cover 1
  (images 002, 003 left half, 004, 005 left half), the red heading traces in
  image-004, the larger gothic hand in image-009, the later cursive on cover 2
  (seen only in the reduced overview image-006; no native tile covers the
  pasted sheet or the spine side of cover 2).
- No span of ten or more connected lines is available anywhere in this packet;
  that reflects the object as photographed.

LIMITATIONS AND SUGGESTED FURTHER IMAGES
- Cover 1 leaf: abrasion and staining have reduced the text to blotches in
  visible light. Raking light, UV or infrared/multispectral imaging of images
  002 and 004's areas would be the obvious next step; the red heading in
  image-004 and the band below it are the most promising targets.
- Spine strip: the left boundary of the notes is where the strip overlaps the
  board leaf; text may continue under the overlap and on the turn-ins inside
  the covers. An image of the inside of the boards/turn-ins would help.
- Cover 2: no native-resolution tile of the pasted sheet with the sideways
  cursive or of the torn spine patch was supplied; a rotated native tile of
  that band is needed before the later inscription can be read.
- Images 009-010 are out of focus and show only line-beginnings; a sharp,
  flattened view of the whole flap (and of the larger-hand leaf behind it)
  would probably allow real reading, since the ink there is well preserved.
- Many readings rest on undivided minims and are given with alternatives.
- This is an unverified image reading. I did nothing beyond the rules: no web
  or search, no files opened other than PROMPT.md and the 10 images of this
  packet.
